title: Surface area from nets
examples: Teacher, how do I find the surface area if the cuboid is hollow?
Does the formula for a prism change if the base is not a rectangle?
Can I use the net to find the volume instead of the surface area?

explain.say: Today we learn about finding surface area using nets. A net is a flat pattern that folds into a 3D shape. We will look at cuboids first.

items: Unfold it into a flat pattern (net)
Calculate the area of the net

explain.say: A cuboid has six rectangular faces. To find its surface area, you must find the area of all six faces. Think of unfolding the box completely flat.

Imagine a cuboid with length four units, width three units, and height two units. You need to calculate the area of each pair of matching sides. The top and bottom are four by three. The front and back are four by two. The two sides are three by two.

The total surface area is two times the area of the length times the width, plus two times the area of the length times the height, plus two times the area of the width times the height. This gives you the total surface area.
Next we look at prisms. A prism has two identical ends, called bases. The sides connecting these bases are rectangles. We find the area of the two bases and add the area of the rectangular sides.
Imagine wrapping a gift box with decorative paper. The paper needs to cover every part of the box. The total paper needed is the box's surface area.

draw.text: Gift wrapping paper covers the surface area.

faq.q: What is a net of a cuboid?
faq.a: A net is simply the flat pattern you cut out that folds up to make the 3D shape. It shows all the faces laid out flat.
asks: How do I see the flat pattern?

faq.q: Do I need to calculate the area of every single face?
faq.a: Yes, you must account for the area of every single face that makes up the outside of the shape. Do not forget any sides.
asks: Should I count all the sides?
Is it enough to find the area of one side?

faq.q: How do I find the surface area of a prism?
faq.a: You find the area of the two identical bases, and then you find the area of the surrounding rectangular sides. You add these three parts together.
asks: What is the formula for a prism surface area?
Do I multiply the base area by two?

faq.q: Can I use the formula 2(lw + lh + wh) for all boxes?
faq.a: No, that specific formula is only for cuboids. Prisms can have different shapes for their bases, like triangles.
asks: Does this work for non-rectangular boxes?

faq.q: If the net is given, do I still need the dimensions?
faq.a: Yes, even if you see the net, you still need the measurements for length, width, and height. You use those numbers to find the area of each section.
asks: Do I measure the net myself?
Are the measurements needed if the net is shown?

facts: A cuboid has six rectangular faces.
Surface area is the total area covering the outside of a 3D object.
The formula for a cuboid's surface area is two times the sum of the products of its three dimensions.
A prism's surface area is the area of its two bases plus its lateral surface area.

quiz.say: A cuboid has dimensions five units, two units, and three units. What is its total surface area?
quiz.why: The formula requires you to calculate two times the area of each pair of opposite faces: five by two, five by three, and two by three.

wrong.1: This answer only calculates the area of the three unique faces once, forgetting to multiply by two for opposite sides.
wrong.2: This answer incorrectly adds the three dimensions together and multiplies by two, which is not the correct area calculation.
wrong.3: This answer only calculates the area of one face from each pair, ignoring the opposite faces entirely.

quiz.say: A triangular prism has a base triangle with an area of ten square units. The three rectangular sides have a combined area of sixty square units. What is the total surface area?
quiz.why: For a prism, you must add the area of the two identical bases to the total area of the rectangular sides.

wrong.0: This answer only uses the area of one base and ignores the rectangular sides completely.
wrong.1: This answer incorrectly doubles the lateral area instead of the base area.
wrong.3: This answer only adds the base area once, forgetting to count the second identical base.

quiz.say: If a cuboid has a length of ten, a width of one, and a height of five, what is the surface area?
quiz.why: You must calculate the area of the top and bottom (ten by one), the front and back (ten by five), and the two sides (one by five), and add them all up.

wrong.0: This answer only adds the three unique face areas together, forgetting to count the opposite faces.
wrong.1: This answer incorrectly adds the three unique face areas and then adds the three dimensions together again.
wrong.3: This answer only calculates the area of the two smallest sides, ignoring the larger faces.
